graph.title: LEGO Friends Advent Calendar 2012 (3316-1)
notes: I am keeping the 206 separate nodes with no edges. This is not a modelling choice. The supplied manual has no assembly steps from which to read connections. Its two pages are the back cover and a Friends product line-up page. Neither shows a parts box or a step picture.

The real set (3316-1) is a 24-door advent calendar, so its booklet really does build many small separate models. Many disconnected groups would be correct for that set. A fully isolated piece, which is what this graph has, would not be.
I won't make up joins to satisfy the connectivity check. Pairing pieces by guesswork would put false connections in the graph. They would also be wrong about which studs, pins or hinges are used.

All 206 pieces from the official parts list are present exactly once, as b1 to b206, with the listed type and colour. Ids follow parts-list order because build order is not visible. new_part_types is empty because every type is in the catalogue.
Once the booklet's step pages are supplied, I will add the joined edges (with method and freedom) and move any sub-assemblies built more than once into repeats.

graph_initial.title: LEGO Friends Advent Calendar 2012 (3316-1)
notes: The attached PDF contains only two pages (back cover and a Friends product line-up page). It has no building steps, so no connections could be read from it. The edge list is empty on purpose, because any joins would be guesses.
All 206 pieces from the official parts list are included as nodes (b1 to b206), with colours as props. Because no build order was visible, ids follow the parts-list order, not build order.
The set is an advent calendar with many small separate mini-builds, one per door. The step pages that would show how they are assembled were not provided.
No repeats were created. Without the steps, it is unclear which sub-assemblies are built more than once.
The pieces appear to be exactly the catalogue types, so new_part_types is empty.
